sources.title: Connecticut DSS Annual Report of Long-Term Care Facility (nursing facility cost reports)
CMS Skilled Nursing Facility All Owners
CMS Skilled Nursing Facility Change of Ownership
CMS Payroll-Based Journal staffing (same months as each cost year)
DSS Nursing Home Rate Setting Guide Book (2024), direct-care definition
CMS Skilled Nursing Facility Cost Report (Medicare cost reports, form CMS-2540-10, public use file)
sources.note: Every US skilled nursing facility, fiscal years ending 2011-2025; used for the national comparison and each home's Medicare cost report.

method.direct_care: Director/assistant directors of nursing + RN + LPN (direct and administrative) + nurse aide salaries (page 10), plus nursing pool fees for RN, LPN and aides (page 13), plus fringe benefits (page 15, lines 1a) allocated by nursing salaries' share of total salaries.
method.nursing_hours: Paid hours reported for the same staff on pages 10 and 13, divided by total resident days (page 8).
method.pbj_same_period: PBJ total nurse hours per resident day for the PBJ quarters that overlap the report period (a full cost year is Q4 through Q3), resident-day weighted.
method.validated: Core figures present, payer days add up to the printed total, and no figure outside a plausible range.
method.raw_food: Raw food cost per resident day = the Raw Food line (page 18, line 2a1, nursing home column) divided by total resident days (page 8). Shown only when the home buys its own food: raw food is at least $3.00 per resident day and contract dietary services (line 2b) are under half of raw food plus contract services. When a food-service company supplies the food, its cost is inside the contract fee and cannot be separated, so only the all-in dietary cost is shown. Raw food may include staff or guest meals where the home reports them in the dietary total (questions G and J on page 18).
method.dietary: All-in dietary cost per resident day = dietary salaries (page 10, lines 5a-5c: dietitian, food service supervisor, dietary workers) + their share of fringe benefits (page 15, allocated by dietary salaries' share of all salaries) + total dietary expenditures (page 18, line 2D: raw food, non-food supplies, other, contract services), divided by total resident days. This compares homes that run their own kitchen with homes that contract it out. Shown only when page 18's lines add up to its printed total.
method.housekeeping: All-in housekeeping cost per resident day = housekeeping salaries (page 10, lines 6a-6b) + their share of fringe benefits + total housekeeping expenditures (page 20, line 4D: supplies and contract services), divided by total resident days.
method.laundry: All-in laundry cost per resident day = laundry salaries (page 10, lines 8a-8b) + their share of fringe benefits + total laundry expenditures (page 19, line 3D: in-house costs and linen or laundry contracts), divided by total resident days.
method.cost_breakdown: Costs by category split the nursing home's total costs (page 27, line 15, nursing-home column) into twelve categories, each divided by total resident days. Fringe benefits (page 15) are part of administrative and general on the form; here they are moved to the staff they belong to, allocated by each group's share of all salaries. Nursing care uses the direct-care definition above. 'All other staff' is the remaining salaries and benefits. 'Other professional fees' is page 13's total less nursing agency. Administrative and general is page 16's total less fringe benefits; management fees (line m12) are part of it. Plant operation is page 22 line 6g (utilities = heat, light and power, water). Building and property is page 22 line 11: rent on leased real property (line 9), depreciation, amortization and property taxes. Interest and insurance are page 27. Shown only when the categories add back to the printed total within 0.2%.
method.medicare_cost_reports: Medicare cost reports (CMS) are filed by each home for its own fiscal year and cover the whole facility (all units), so they do not match the DSS nursing-home column exactly. Figures are per total day on the Medicare report: operating expense, salaries, wage-related costs (benefits), contract labor and net patient revenue. Operating margin = (net patient revenue - operating expense) / net patient revenue. National and Connecticut medians use full-year reports only (360-371 days), grouped by the year the fiscal year ends, and leave out implausible values.
method.related_party_rent: Rent or lease paid to related parties is the cost the home reported on page 4 for related parties whose description mentions rent, lease, realty or real estate. It is already inside the building and property category, not in addition to it.
method.support_costs_exclude: None of the support figures include management-company charges reported on page 16, kitchen or laundry equipment depreciation and building costs (property), or utilities; a contractor's fee includes its own overhead and profit.
method.part_year: The report covers fewer than 360 days (the home opened, closed or changed owner). Dates come from the report's certification page. Part-year filings are left out of the statewide medians.

caveats: Figures are as reported by each nursing home on its Connecticut DSS 'Annual Report of Long-Term Care Facility' for the cost year ending September 30. They are the home's own filing, before DSS audit or rate-setting adjustments, and are not Medicaid-allowable costs.
Figures were read from the published PDFs by software. Scanned reports were read with OCR. Each figure is checked against the totals printed on the same report; figures that fail a check are marked.

Direct care follows the DSS rate-setting definition: nursing and nurse-aide salaries, related fringe benefits, and nursing pool (agency) costs. Fringe benefits are not reported by job, so the direct-care share of fringe is allocated in proportion to nursing salaries.
Owner, officer and related-party names, addresses and amounts are shown as written on the report and in CMS ownership data. Addresses may be business or personal addresses as filed.
Being listed as an owner or related party is not an allegation of wrongdoing. Spending figures are not a measure of care quality.
corrections_notice: Records come from public state and federal sources. To report an error, email hello@danbeem.xyz.
cost_categories: Nursing care (nursing and aide staff, agency, their benefits)
Dietary (kitchen staff, benefits, food, supplies, contracts)
All other staff and their benefits (administration, maintenance, activities, social work, therapy staff, etc.)
Other professional fees (therapy, medical director, consultants and other fees in lieu of salaries)
Administrative and general, non-salary (management fees, legal, accounting, office, advertising, etc.)
Resident care supplies and services (drugs, medical supplies, oxygen, lab, recreation)
Plant operation and utilities (repairs, heat, light and power, water, equipment leases)
Building and property (rent, depreciation, amortization, property taxes)
